question: ‘Milind Panho’ is a post-Mauryan text which contains the conversations between the Indo-Greek ruler Menander and the scholar and Buddhist monk ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagasena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Milind Panho’** is a post-Mauryan text written in the form of a dialogue or conversation between the Indo-Greek king **Menander I (Milinda)** and the Buddhist monk **Nagasena**. This statement is *correct*.
 
• The text is an important work in Buddhist literature and is considered a classic in Pali literature. It is a unique blend of Indian and Hellenistic thought.
 
• The text is primarily a philosophical discourse where **Nagasena** answers various questions posed by **Menander** related to Buddhist philosophy, ethics, and metaphysical issues. *This is correct.*
 
• The text is significant for its role in spreading Buddhism beyond India, particularly to the Hellenistic world during the post-Mauryan period. It highlights the interaction between Indian and Greek cultures.
 
• The **Milind Panho** is divided into seven books, each focusing on different aspects of Buddhist teachings and philosophy.
 
• **Nagasena’s arguments** in the text are seen as a masterful exposition of Buddhist thought, and the work remains influential in Buddhist studies.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Nagasena.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Nagasena:**

 
 
• **Nagasena** was a Buddhist monk and scholar who played a vital role in explaining and spreading Buddhist teachings during the post-Mauryan era.
 
• He was known for his sharp intellect and ability to explain complex philosophical concepts in simple terms.
 
 
 
• **Menander I (Milinda):**
 
 
• Menander I was an Indo-Greek king who ruled during the 2nd century BCE. His kingdom included parts of modern-day Afghanistan, Pakistan, and northern India.
 
• Menander I is remembered for his patronage of Buddhism. After his interactions with Nagasena, it is believed that he converted to Buddhism and became a great supporter of the religion.
 
 
 
• **Features of Milind Panho:**
 
 
• The text is written in the form of a dialogue, which was a common method of teaching and explaining philosophical ideas in ancient India.
 
• It includes discussions on topics such as the nature of self, karma, rebirth, and the path to enlightenment.
 
• The text also highlights the cultural and intellectual exchanges between the Indian and Greek civilizations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Explained:**

 
 
• **Badarayana:** He was an ancient Indian philosopher and the author of the **Brahma Sutras**, a foundational text of Vedanta philosophy. He was not related to the Milind Panho.
 
• **Patanjali:** He was the author of the **Yoga Sutras**, which form the basis of classical yoga philosophy. He is not connected to the Milind Panho.
 
• **Kapila:** He was an ancient Indian sage and the founder of the **Samkhya school of philosophy**. There is no connection between him and the Milind Panho.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Milind Panho:**
 
 
• It serves as a historical document showcasing the interaction between Hellenistic and Indian cultures during the post-Mauryan period.
 
• The text is an important source for understanding Buddhist philosophy and its spread beyond India.
